other_items.note: STRUCTURAL. Amplitude scales as 1/(omega*C) and this world's year is half Earth's, so 50 m damps seasonality about twice as hard as Earth's ocean does. Coldest-month mean is what PFT survival gates on. One perturbation run, ever, gives a permanent scaling for every later result.

other_items.item: Penman over a dry land column
other_items.note: Validated over ocean, where the air is equilibrated with the surface. Over a subgrid lake the column is dry, so VPD is too high, E is overstated and the verdict under-carves. Opposite in sign to the albedo-driven over-carve, and the only item here whose magnitude is unknown.

Aerosols are off entirely (L_AERO = 0), and ExoPlaSim 3.4.2 cannot switch them on: radmod.f90 declares aero_nl but never reads it, so l_aerorad is pinned at 0. Reported upstream. Magnitude bounded on a DRY source area of about 12% of land. SIGN RESOLVED 2026-08-16 and it is cooling. Aerosol forcing reverses sign at a critical surface albedo a_c; Mie over the Balkanski source distribution, band-averaged on the k25v spectrum with measured indices (Di Biagio 2019 below 0.95 um, Rocha-Lima 2018 Fig. 10 digitised above), gives a_c = 0.50 in band 1 and 0.51-0.57 in band 2. Salt crust tops out at 0.50, so every surface here sits below a_c -- narrowly at the bright end. Evaporite source mineralogy is less absorbing than the Saharan silicate measured, which widens the margin. Two earlier claims here were wrong: OPAC is 1.0-2.1x more absorbing than measured in the near-IR, not 8-22x (the ARIA Peters file used for that comparison is the outlier), and the two-sided entry that replaced the original one-signed one was itself an overcorrection. The original bracket was still one-signed BY CONSTRUCTION, which is the defect worth remembering. See notes/dust.md.
